decisive_items: Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
Acute stratum corneum present overlying full thickness epithelial necrosis
response.rationale: Generalized atypical target lesions, blisters, fever, and full-thickness epidermal necrosis on biopsy are diagnostic of Stevens-Johnson syndrome; SLE and ACLE explain the background malar rash/serologies but not the acute necrotic targetoid eruption.

rejected.why: Runner-up; explains malar/photo-sensitive lupus features but not generalized full-thickness epidermal necrosis.
SLE is the underlying disease but too broad for the acute targetoid blistering syndrome.
Thrombocytopenia is a lab feature of SLE, not the presenting diagnosis.
No renal-specific evidence; anemia and hypocomplementemia do not establish lupus nephritis.
